title: SS27 Boys' Knit Fabric Direction
summary: Boys' knits: cotton jersey, piqué, micro-mesh, terry and UPF-rated swim and performance fabrics.
research_period: Pitti Bimbo 103, Florence, 24-25 June 2026; Playtime Paris, 28-30 June 2026; analysis July to November 2026
markets: Premium and mid-market childrenswear, Europe-led fairs, global retail

sections.heading: The evidence
sections.body:
- Fatamadrina lists lightweight linen, voile, organic cotton, terry and micro-mesh as SS27 fabrics<sup>[1]</sup>
- Swimwear, T-shirts and accessories with built-in UV filters were prominent and are becoming common, linked to family concern for health and to changing climate<sup>[2]</sup>
- Teeter Totter showed UPF50+ swim and sportswear, backpacks and ultra-light, sand-free beach towels<sup>[3]</sup>
- Newer lines emphasise breathability, quick drying and comfort; childrenswear is moving toward functionality, material quality and durability<sup>[2]</sup>

sections.heading: Fabric by fabric
sections.body:
| Knit | Hand | Uses |
|---|---|---|
| Organic cotton jersey | Soft | Tees |
| Piqué | Structured | Polos |
| Micro-mesh | Airy | Sport tops, linings |
| Terry | Absorbent | Shorts, cover-ups |
| UPF swim and performance | Stretch, quick-dry | Swim, rash guards |

design_implications:
- Test UPF after stretching and wetting.
- Safety: no drawstrings or long cords at the hood, neck or waist, in line with EN 14682; test the attachment strength of buttons, snaps and decorations, and keep small detachable parts off baby and toddler pieces.
